what_happened: The laptop's lid was closed while the answers were being made. Two answer calls were under way, one after the other. Each was cut as a timeout when the laptop woke, although its reply had come back, and was asked again. The second reply is the answer that was kept and judged. No answer, context or score is changed by this correction: only times.

rule.text:
A try of a model call is one the machine slept under when all three hold:
  1. it ended as a timeout;
  2. it lasted longer than its own timeout (a call that is running is cut at its timeout, so a
     longer one was not running the whole time);
  3. the low-power time the machine itself logged inside the try's start and end is at least the
     try's overrun past its timeout.
The seconds recorded for such a try are taken out of the three sums they went into: the row's
generator.time_s and generator.retry_s, the row's timing.wall_s, and the wall_s of that start in
the run manifest. What those sums hold afterwards: the try that answered, the pause the harness
waits before it tries again, and the harness's own overhead. The slept try's own share of awake
seconds, in which its reply came back, cannot be told apart from the sleep by the run's clock and
goes out with it.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: generator.attempts is 2 and generator.calls is 1 in these rows: two requests were made and paid for, one answer was kept.
The tokens of the discarded reply are listed under slept_tries. They are not part of the row's token counts, which are those of the try that answered.
The try that answered read the prompt from the cache the first try had written (generator.cached_input_tokens), which no other row of this run does.
started_at, finished_at and answered_at are clock times and have the sleep between them.

judge_calls_with_logged_low_power_time_i.note: No change is made to these. Whether the call was held while the machine was in this state is not known from the record, so its seconds stand as recorded.
